title: Upper-limb elbow-centered motor imagery dataset (10 classes)
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 12 healthy participants performing upper-limb motor imagery tasks centered on elbow movements. Participants executed kinesthetic imagery of nine goal-directed tasks (elbow flexion, drawer opening, soup preparation, weight lifting, door opening, plate cleaning, combing, pizza cutting, and pick-and-place) plus rest, cued by visual stimuli. The dataset contains 330 trials recorded at 1000 Hz using 17 EEG channels and is intended for brain-computer interface research and motor imagery classification studies.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired from 12 naive participants using an EGI Geodesic Net Amps 400 series amplifier with 17 Ag/AgCl sponge electrodes sampled at 1000 Hz. Online bandpass filtering (0.1-40 Hz) was applied during acquisition. The experimental paradigm consisted of 15 runs per subject, each containing 24 trials (4 rest + 4 elbow flexion + 2 each of 8 goal-directed tasks). Each trial included a 4-6 s randomized visual cue presentation followed by 4-6 s of rest. Participants performed kinesthetic motor imagery without actual movement.
